body:
This change seems a bit aggressive to me. If any axis is within the range of the volume, then we calculate then we are applying the volume to the entire froxel buffer. This will have a huge performance impact as it will significantly reduce the situations where froxels are culled. 

Would it perhaps make more sense to change this to three conditions (one for each axis) and then only change the range for the corresponding axis?
I'll admit that I made this change without really understanding exactly what the math is doing. Your suggestion seems good though, I'll give it a try and see what happens.

I made a minimal reproduction project for this bug: https://github.com/AshbyGeek/godot-fog-reproduction.

I also made a gif of both the old (godot 4.4 dev 4) behavior:
![godot-fog-recreation-old-behavior](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0690b4ff-f0d4-48c0-ada7-d8150616ca4c)

and the correct behavior based on commit 2e6ff1081f9a3869570ae09b58a47a06db185620 of this PR:
![godot-fog-recreation-correct-behavior](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a51a2463-9faf-4fad-81e0-6aaf14673cfb)
